sources.citation: Grambank (Grambank Consortium), language page Siawi siaw1243, coded by Harald Hammarström from Krieg 2005.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only confirms Krieg 2005 'Siawi grammar writeup' as the classification source; Grambank has no stress feature and the datapoint table is JS-rendered.

sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon (ed.). TransNewGuinea.org, language page 'Siawi' (alias Musan).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lexicon sourced solely from Conrad & Dye (1975); no stress marking, no prosodic notes.

sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'Siawi language' (stub; 'Musan language' redirects to it) and 'Amto-Musan languages' (raw wikitext, 2026-09-17).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Stub: 'Siawi' is a misspelling of the endonym Siafli, 'Musan' a clan name (ISO CR 2007-176); one grammar line from Krieg 2005 (postpositions, SV order, clause-final polar interrogative particle). No phonology, no stress. The family page gives cognate and loan tables from Foley 2018 and Conrad & Dye 1975 only.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212 (pp. 196-197).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Amto-Musan [amt, mmp]: Linda Krieg et al. of the New Tribes Mission is in the process of translating the Bible into Siawi, also known as Musan, and so far, has produced unpublished phonemic and grammar sketch write-ups (p.c. Linda Krieg 2007).' Confirms an unpublished phonemic write-up exists; says nothing about its content.

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project. 2010. Siawi Swadesh List (archive.org item rosettaproject_mmp_swadesh-1, CC-BY).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: About 100 items, each in an orthographic-style and an IPA transcription (grave/diaeresis mark vowel quality, e.g. tèwane = tɛwane; backslash = glottal stop). Forms match the Conrad & Dye 1975 Musan list (sɪsʌmo, piowarɛ, kepiyɔ, tʌbɛki). No stress marks, no source note, nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record siaw1243 (JSON) with Glottolog's most extensive description list; reference records 318431 (Krieg 2005) and 86509 (Krieg 1992).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Glottolog's most extensive descriptions: Krieg 2005 'Siawi grammar writeup' (ms., 44 pp., grammar sketch, flagged nosharefn =, i.e. held by Hammarström but not distributable); Krieg 1992 'Tienesi [Siawi Genesis]' (NTM Goroka, 139 pp., listed by Glottolog as a text collection, a scripture translation despite the 'phonology or text collection' Glottolog's most extensive description label); Conrad & Dye 1975 and Laycock 1973 a wordlist or less. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area (Pacific Linguistics D-90).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists for Siawi only New Tribes Mission 1992 readers and scripture (Tienesi/Genesis 139 pp., Ukowolelele reader 3 vols, animals reader 26 pp.), wrongly located 'Okapa area?'; for Musan/Musian only Voegelins 1965 and Wurm & Hattori 1981. No linguistic description listed.

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & T. Wayne Dye. 1975. Some language relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18 (Pacific Linguistics A-40), 1-35. DOI 10.15144/PL-A40.1.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.2 Amto-Musan Family (pp. 19-20): Musan ~150 speakers in an uncensused village east of Amto; 29% cognates with Amto; sound correspondences; nothing on phonology or stress. The paper's only stress statement, 'Contrastive word stress was noted in Ama, and possibly in Rocky Peak, Bo, and Owiniga' (Figure C, Summary of Arai Phonology, p. 15), concerns the Arai/Left May family, not Musan. Musan otherwise appears only as a column of the comparative wordlists (no stress marks).

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification (Pacific Linguistics B-25), entry 210 Musian. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The earlier Amto reader reports entry 210 says 'little other structural information is extractable from the data'; kept only for completeness, since it is the earliest record of the language (a copy is already held).

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. New Guinea World, 'Arai and Samaia Rivers' / 'Samaia River' / 'Siawi' / 'Musan' pages (newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Siawi' and 'samaia-river' topics 'do not exist yet'; the 'Musan' page is an empty heading ('====== Musan ======'). No data.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher record (DOI); no open copy and no library e-access found (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: The only modern handbook treatment of Amto-Musan (the earlier scan named it). Snippet probes suggest its Amto-Musan section is lexical/classificatory, but only reading pp. ~320-330 (Amto-Musan) would settle whether Foley gives any phonological remarks on Siawi drawn from Krieg's data.

sources.citation: Krieg, Linda. 2005. Siawi grammar writeup. Ms. 44 pp. (New Tribes Mission / Ethnos360; copy in Harald Hammarström's collection, Glottolog 318431, coded for Grambank).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked; the linked copy was not accessible when a reader tried
sources.note: The only grammatical description of Siawi that exists; a 44-page sketch of this kind normally opens with a phonology summary that would state where stress falls. Glottolog marks the file non-shareable, so it would have to be requested from Hammarström or from the author/Ethnos360.

sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. 1982. Papuan Languages of Oceania. Tübingen: Gunter Narr. (Section on the Amto-Musian family, ch. 11.)

sources.note: Snippet shows a paragraph on the 'Amto-Musian (Musan) phylum-level Family' citing Conrad & Dye 1975; the preceding typological lines (nasal vowels, 'tone may be present') belong to a neighbouring family, so this is a low-yield check only.

sources.note: Early survey wordlists including Amto and, per Carrington 1996, the Amanab-area languages; unlikely to mark stress but it is the earliest published data on the Samaia River languages.

sources.citation: Krieg, Linda. n.d. (before 2007). Siawi phonemic write-up. Unpublished ms., New Tribes Mission, Papua New Guinea (reported in Hammarström 2010: 196-197 from p.c. Linda Krieg 2007).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: A dedicated phonemic description is the document most likely to contain an explicit stress statement (NTM/SIL phonology write-ups routinely have a 'suprasegmentals' section). Not catalogued anywhere online; existence known only from Hammarström's personal communication.

sources.citation: Frawley, William (ed.). 2003. International Encyclopedia of Linguistics, 2nd ed., entry 'Amto-Musan languages'; Wurm, Stephen A. 1982. Papuan Languages of Oceania (Narr), Amto-Musian family paragraph.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.access_detail: only an abstract or snippet reachable
sources.note: IEL entry is a two-line stub ('Siawi, Siafli. 200 speakers.. Musan: also called Musian, Musa'); Wurm 1982 snippet gives only the Conrad & Dye classification. Neither says anything about Siawi stress in the visible snippets.

sources.citation: Catalogue probes: OLAC (language-archives.org/language/mmp), Endangered Languages Project lang/10683, SIL PNG resources for mmp, Ethnologue mmp, PARADISEC languages/mmp, HathiTrust full-text search, ScriptureEarth mmp, archive.org and Crossref searches.
sources.note: OLAC refused the connection; ELP, SIL, Ethnologue, PARADISEC and HathiTrust returned an automated-access block/JS challenge pages or 403; archive.org search found only the Rosetta wordlist and Wikipedia dumps; Crossref returned nothing relevant. No Siawi phonology surfaced anywhere.
